small_guidance:
- Expand the autotune key to include POW so different problem sizes pick distinct configs; also add a few configs with `BLOCK_OC` as a tunable (currently fixed to next_pow2(OC)=16, which is fine here but constrains warp use). Try `num_warps=2, BLOCK_SP=32` and `num_warps=4, BLOCK_SP=64` more aggressively — current optimum likely sits there.
- Hoist `w_vals` loads: weights are tiny (3·16·27 floats); preload the full weight tile per (ic, kd, kh, kw) outside the spatial loop using `tl.static_range`, or load all weights once into registers indexed by static loop vars to avoid 81 separate gmem loads per program.
- Use `tl.multiple_of` / `tl.max_contiguous` hints on `iw` so the contiguous-W loads are recognized as vectorizable.
large_guidance:
- Consider swapping the parallelization: one program per (N, pd, ph) tile producing all OC×POW outputs in registers — this amortizes the 81 weight loads across more output points and keeps weights resident.
- Try a channels-last (NDHWC) input/output layout so the IC=3 axis is innermost; then the inner `ic` loop becomes a small dot product the compiler can vectorize, and `x_val` loads coalesce across IC.
- Alternative: implement an explicit GEMM formulation — gather an im2col-like tile of shape (BLOCK_SP, IC·KD·KH·KW) against weight (IC·KD·KH·KW, OC) using `tl.dot`, which on Ada will hit tensor cores (TF32) and likely beat the current FMA loop substantially.
